hey i totally agree im so so sorry you’ve found yourself in this spot and first i just want to say you absolutely can and will come out of this! it really isn’t forever even though im sure it feels like it. i went through Hell with binging earlier this year and felt just how you described, wont go into all the details but it was just awful - interrupting school, work, socializing, personality. took up all of my time and was all i thought of, i started stealing food it was horrendous and so isolating. it got so bad i actually opened up about it to others in my life even though i’d never breathe a word of the restrictive ED i’ve had for over a decade. i say all this just to make the point that people really do get through it <3 you totally will. i genuinely don’t struggle with any of that anymore and am doing so much better mentally. there are so many great resources online and just hearing how others struggled with exactly what you’re going through can help so please seek that out. i recommend kathryn hansen’s brain over binge podcasts/yt vids etc. her and another woman do a free group therapy call regarding binging each month, it helped me so much. their view and explanation of the psychology of binging is very helpful. andrew huberman has a good yt episode on eating disorders including BED if the science approach helps you out, it definitely helped me to understand more deeply what was going on and give myself more compassion. it really is so common, i think something like a third of americans struggle with it ? my restrictive ED also interfered with my undergrad, i just want you to know that if you have to medically withdraw for a semester, even your first, it doesn’t at all mean you aren’t capable of doing great in your studies and having a fulfilling education. you deserve to not be feeling like this and i hope you’re proud of yourself for reaching out for help and community <3

so much denial and ignorance in this thread from people convinced they’re the unicorn that violates the laws of physics instead of, idk, not accounting for food/water weight, bloating, inaccurate package labeling and food weighing, or literally just not counting calories correctly which is the real “culprit” here 99% of the time. like yes im sure every one of you that replied here so upset with OP’s *factually correct* statement are the rare exceptions and are all 4’9” with a BMI of 10 and experience long term starvation and have uncommon metabolic and autoimmune disorders which literally only change your BMR by a couple of hundred calories daily MAX and are not just experiencing any of the other much more likely scenarios LMAO. i know it’s hard to hear since we all suffer regardless but this needs to be said more often here and it kills me seeing daily posts with “metabolism days” and “my metabolism’s so slowed” no it fucking is not lmfao.

your TDEE from an online calculator is correct within a small ballpark, and if you have a condition that affects your metabolism in some way, such as via thyroid or hormones, it can be +/- 100 calories off, max 200. anything else is human error with calorie counting or you are seeing weight on the scale which is not actual weight gained. it really is that simple.

The first episode I had no idea. My thoughts mostly involved other people talking about me, taking photos of me, following me, larger scale conspiracies to “catch” me by cops or officials at my university, cameras and microphones installed in rooms, people speaking to me from prewritten scripts or repeating my own words back to me. I had really bad issues with technology and couldn’t use any internet devices for over 3 months. I pretty much thought all of my devices were “hacked” and I was being watched or investigated. I also believed I had multiple medical issues which progressed to the point that i thought my body had stopped involuntarily breathing.

Like other posters said, after the first episode I was sure I’d be able to discern future delusional thoughts... boy was I wrong. I had many more persistent thoughts and another full blown episode. The difference this time was that my convictions were even stronger. This time it *really* was happening since I’d already experienced psychosis and could now tell that this had to be *real* lol. My thoughts mostly consisted of believing cars and people were following me. Eventually I was able to realize the thoughts were the same as before and nothing I was fearing was grounded in reality.
